"""Polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to SAT."""

def reduce(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # k < 0: no vertex cover of negative size -> unsatisfiable formula.
    if k < 0:
        return {"num_vars": 0, "clauses": [[]]}

    # Edge clauses: every edge must have a chosen endpoint.
    clauses = [[u + 1, v + 1] for u, v in edges]

    # k >= n: all vertices form a cover, so the edge clauses alone are satisfiable.
    if k >= n:
        return {"num_vars": n, "clauses": clauses}

    # k == 0: no vertex may be chosen.
    if k == 0:
        clauses.extend([[-v] for v in range(1, n + 1)])
        return {"num_vars": n, "clauses": clauses}

    # 1 <= k < n. Sequential-counter encoding of "at most k of x_1..x_n are true".
    num_vars = n + (n - 1) * k

    def s(i, j):
        # 1 <= i <= n-1, 1 <= j <= k
        return n + (i - 1) * k + j

    # x_i -> s_{i,1}
    for i in range(1, n):
        clauses.append([-i, s(i, 1)])

    # s_{i-1,j} -> s_{i,j}
    for i in range(2, n):
        for j in range(1, k + 1):
            clauses.append([-s(i - 1, j), s(i, j)])

    # x_i and s_{i-1,j-1} -> s_{i,j}
    for i in range(2, n):
        for j in range(2, k + 1):
            clauses.append([-i, -s(i - 1, j - 1), s(i, j)])

    # x_i and s_{i-1,k} -> false (would mean k+1 chosen)
    for i in range(2, n + 1):
        clauses.append([-i, -s(i - 1, k)])

    return {"num_vars": num_vars, "clauses": clauses}
